title: Algorithmic Opacity as a Principal-Agent Problem
abstract: arXiv:2611.17980v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Concerns about gaming and trade secrecy, frequently invoked to justify algorithmic opacity, can also mask self-serving strategic behavior by decision-makers, who may prioritize private benefits over social welfare. We develop a principal-agent test for when algorithmic decision-making should trigger disclosure obligations even when concerns about gaming or trade secrecy exist. The test, which is anchored in decision quality, relies on two diagnostics that can be disclosed without enabling gaming or revealing trade secrets: the error profile (false positive and false negative rates, overall and for each group) and the distribution of decision outcomes across groups. These diagnostics make visible whether decision-makers align design and implementation with the public interest or instead use opacity to obscure bias, inefficiency, or strategic shirking. translated_title: 算法不透明性作为委托-代理问题
translated_abstract: 对博弈操纵和商业秘密的担忧经常被用来为算法不透明性辩护，但这些担忧也可能掩盖决策者自利的策略性行为——他们可能将私人利益置于社会福利之上。我们开发了一种委托-代理检验方法，用于判断即使存在博弈操纵或商业秘密的顾虑，算法决策何时仍应触发披露义务。该检验以决策质量为基础，依赖于两项可在不助长博弈操纵或不泄露商业秘密的前提下披露的诊断指标：错误概况（假阳性率和假阴性率，包括总体水平和各群体分别的水平）以及各群体间决策结果的分布。这些诊断指标能够揭示决策者是否使算法的设计与实施符合公共利益，还是相反地利用不透明性来掩盖偏见、低效或策略性推诿。社会群体间的显著差异以及决策结果分布的不对称性……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出基于委托-代理理论的检验框架，主张即使存在博弈操纵和商业秘密的顾虑，算法决策者也应披露错误概况和群体间决策结果分布这两项诊断指标，以防止其利用不透明性掩盖偏见、低效或损害公共利益的策略性行为。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a principal-agent test arguing that even when gaming and trade secrecy concerns exist, algorithmic decision-makers should disclose two diagnostics—the error profile and the cross-group distribution of decision outcomes—to prevent opacity from masking bias, inefficiency, or strategic shirking.
